body: @AThousandShips I've reorderd the description and added an MRP that demonstrates the deadlock. Did I miss anything?

I can confirm this on **4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf]**, on real hardware with the default pool size, and on a desktop. In our case a **loading worker thread** (not the main thread) holds `singleton_mutex`, but it is the same lock and the same wait.

**Quest 3** (Horizon OS build 52433670048800520, Adreno 740, Vulkan Mobile, 6 worker threads, low-priority ratio 0.34): a Quest 3 VR app froze for good at a scene start that loads three GLB models and a scene with `load_threaded_request(..., use_sub_threads = true)`, in **3 of 3** first sessions (no shader cache, no pipeline cache). The main thread and all 6 pool threads sat in `futex_wait`, and their CPU times did not change. In later sessions, with a cache that already held those shaders, the same start did not freeze.

**Windows 11, RTX 5090, official 4.7.2 editor binary, Mobile renderer:** the same app path with an empty user folder, `max_threads = 6`, `low_priority_thread_ratio = 0.34` and the process held to **one CPU core** froze in 9 of 11 runs (0 of 3 on all cores). A synthetic project with no app code (24 scenes, 288 `StandardMaterial3D`s each with its own shader, two threaded loads at a time with no sub-threads, ratio 0.5, one core) froze in **5 of 5** runs, after 3 to 7 of the 24 files.

The full dumps of the frozen desktop runs (the official build has no symbols, so we labelled return addresses by the error strings near them, and matched the lock address `0xac68ee0` to code that only `scene_shader_forward_mobile.cpp` uses) all show:

| Thread | Stack | Waits for |
|---|---|---|
| 1 pool thread | threaded load: `parse_variant` -> `ArrayMesh::_set_surfaces()` -> `get_vertex_input_mask()` -> `get_shader_variant()` -> `ShaderRD::_compile_version_end()` | the new shader's compile group (`wait_for_group_task_completion()`), while it holds `singleton_mutex` |
| the other 5 pool threads | `PipelineCompilation`: `ShaderData::_create_pipeline()` -> `get_shader_variant()` | `singleton_mutex` |
| main thread | `RenderingServer.get_rendering_info()` -> `SceneShaderForwardMobile::get_pipeline_compilations()` | `singleton_mutex` |

The synthetic project's dump has the same shape: two load threads in `ArrayMesh::_set_surfaces()` (one in `get_vertex_input_mask()`, one in `is_valid()` via `mesh_generate_pipelines()`), and four pool threads in `_create_pipeline()` / `version_get_shader()`.

The compile group is posted at the end of the pool's FIFO queue (`shader_rd.cpp:735`, `worker_thread_pool.cpp:252`, `205-214`). Pipeline compile tasks that were queued before it (each new mesh queues high-priority ubershader compiles, `render_forward_mobile.cpp:3343`) take the free threads first and block on the lock. Once every pool thread blocks, the group never runs.

PR #123312 (merged into `master` for 4.8) removes exactly this: `get_shader_variant()` and `is_valid()` no longer hold `singleton_mutex` around the `ShaderRD` calls. We have not run `master`, but the cycle above cannot form there in this way. Could #123312 be linked to this issue and **considered for a 4.7 cherry-pick**? On standalone VR it hangs the first session after an install, and the user can only quit the app.

Workaround on 4.7.2 that held in our tests (0 of 4 freezes on the Quest on the same path, 0 of 24 desktop runs on one core, 0 of 14 runs of the synthetic project):
- load files that can contain meshes one at a time, with `ResourceLoader.load()` inside one high-priority `WorkerThreadPool` group task (so the dependencies load in that thread, no sub-threads);
- in that task, first add a no-op high-priority task and `wait_for_task_completion()` on it, so every task that was queued before has started (the lock is free) before the load begins;
- export with the shader baker: on 4.7.2 a baked shader loads from the cache and posts no compile group (`shader_rd.cpp:723-729`), so nothing waits under the lock for it.

It does not cover the main thread case of this issue (`_geometry_instance_add_surface()` -> `is_valid()` at `render_forward_mobile.cpp:3011`, `3031`, `3053`), except where the baker covers the shader.
